So each face of the big cube is a 2×2 checkerboard of black and white squares. Moreover, the coloring must be consistent with the "alternating black and white cubes" arrangement: the 8 unit cubes are colored alternately (like a 3D checkerboard), and each face of the big cube shows a 2×2 checkerboard pattern. Importantly, adjacent faces must match at edges: the color of a unit square on a face corresponds to the color of the unit cube at that position. Each unit cube is entirely black or entirely white, so the face pattern is determined: the cube at position (i,j,k) (i,j,k ∈ {0,1}) is black if i+j+k is even (say), white otherwise. Then each face shows a checkerboard.

Now, the net: cross-shaped net with 6 faces, each face a 2×2 of black/white squares. We need to determine which net folds into a painted cube consistent with the checkerboard cube coloring.

Key property: on the actual cube, at each corner of the big cube, three faces meet. The unit cube at that corner is either black or white, so the three face-squares at that corner (one on each face) all have the same color. So the condition: when the net is folded, at each of the 8 corners of the cube, the three squares meeting at that corner must all be the same color.
